newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish 1996 state deficit fell to FIM 36.8 bln.
newsitem.headline: Finnish 1996 state deficit fell to FIM 36.8 bln.

text.p: The Finnish central government deficit or net borrowing requirement fell in 1996 by 22.1 billion markka from the previous year to 36.8 billion markka, the finance ministry said on Thursday.
State net borrowing totalled 34.5 billion markka in 1996, the ministry said, adding that the rest of the 36.8 billion markka need was covered by unwinding reserves.

"The net borrowing need of state finances contracted last year by 22.1 billion markka," the ministry said, adding this was possible because state revenue rose and the rise in expenditure came to a halt.
State revenue excluding borrowing increased 14 percent year-on-year to 173.9 billion markka, while expenditure, excluding debt amortisation, fell 0.3 percent to 210.7 billion markka.

On the expenditure side, interest on state debt rose 16 percent to nearly 30 billion markka. State transfers to municipalities fell 16 percent to 33 billion markka, transfers to industry and business fell five percent to 18 billion and transfers to households fell five percent to 40 billion.
Spending on new defence material increased 22 percent to 3.7 billion markka and state pension pay-outs rose nearly four percent to 12.5 billion.
On the revenue side, income and property tax revenue ballooned 21 percent to 46 billion markka and value-added tax revenue rose 14 percent to 42 billion. @
Fuel tax revenue was up nine percent at 12.7 billion markka, and alcoholic beverages and tobacco tax revenue both rose close to three percent to seven billion and 3.2 billion respectively.
Booming private car sales generated 3.6 billion markka in automobile tax revenue last year, up over 34 percent on 1995, the finance ministry said.
